slides.say: Two cyclists start together from the same point of a circular track one point two kilometers long, and ride in opposite directions. Their speeds are twenty and sixteen kilometers per hour. After how many minutes do they meet for the first time?
So they ride toward each other around the track. They ask when they first meet, in minutes.
at: They ask when they first meet

slides.say: We'll solve it in two different ways. Let's start with the math way, like in the lesson. In opposite directions, they meet when together they have covered one full lap, one point two kilometers.
at: together they have covered one full lap

slides.say: They move toward each other, so we add the speeds. Twenty plus sixteen is thirty-six kilometers per hour.
So we need the time for one lap at thirty-six kilometers per hour.
The time is one point two divided by thirty-six. We multiply both by ten, so it's twelve over three hundred sixty. That's one thirtieth of an hour.
at: The time is one point two divided by thirty-six
so it's twelve over three hundred

slides.say: A thirtieth of sixty minutes is two minutes.
Eighteen, choice number one, is the same-direction answer. It subtracts the speeds, but here they ride toward each other.
at: here they ride toward each other

slides.say: [pause] Now by understanding, with identical ratios. We start again from the givens. Together they cover twenty plus sixteen, thirty-six kilometers in sixty minutes.
We need one lap, one point two kilometers. Thirty-six divided by thirty is one point two. So we divide by thirty.
So the time is divided by thirty too. Sixty divided by thirty is two minutes.
Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
